story_type: sea turtle freed from fishing gear offshore
hook: An 800 pound turtle, tangled in a buoy line 30 miles out
narration: This eight hundred pound sea turtle was tangled in a buoy line, thirty miles offshore.
A passing boat spotted it off South Jersey and called it in.
A loop of line from the buoy had wrapped around one of its flippers.
A Coast Guard crew from Cape May carried a stranding team out to it.
Leatherbacks breathe air, so a turtle pinned to fishing gear can drown.
Their turtle expert had always freed animals from a distance, with line cutters. This time he went hands on.
The crew leaned over the side and held the turtle against the boat.
Its shell alone was more than five and a half feet long.
outcome: They freed its flipper, and the turtle safely swam away.
title: 800 pound turtle tangled 30 miles out

description:
On Aug. 9, 2014, a Coast Guard Station Cape May crew and the Marine Mammal Stranding Center freed an approximately 800 pound leatherback turtle entangled in fishing gear 30 miles off South Jersey. Once freed, the turtle swam away.
